segments.title: 第80章 信封戰爭
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 80: The Envelope War

As it approached one in the afternoon, Duan Qintian glanced at the time and said from the lectern, "Students who have finished writing their letters can start delivering them. Afterward, if you have something to do this afternoon, just let me know and you can head home."

As soon as he said this, many people stood up.

Some classmates who had joined the club together began handing their letters to each other.

There were also bolder boys who walked up to Ying Chanxi's desk, held a letter out to her, and then turned to leave, somewhat embarrassed.

Ying Chanxi was still writing her second letter. She looked up to see a letter appear before her, blinked, and said a polite "thank you" before lowering her head to continue writing.

But soon, another letter appeared in front of Ying Chanxi.

Liu Shaowen appeared by her desk with a smile, handing a letter to Ying Chanxi. "Class President, this is for you."

After saying that, as if afraid his intention was too obvious, he added, "We're the only two from our class here, and I don't know anyone else..."

As he spoke, Liu Shaowen took out another envelope and handed it to Li Luo. "It just so happens your cousin is here too, so I'll entrust them to you."

With that, Liu Shaowen waved and left, appearing very casual.

He thought he had handled it quite smoothly, but Li Luo was at a loss for whether to laugh or cry as he looked at the letter from Liu Shaowen on his desk.

Although he had fantasized that someone other than Ying Chanxi might give him a letter, shouldn't it at least be a girl?

What was this about a guy giving him a letter?

This Liu Shaowen was truly ridiculous, trying to cover up his intentions... Even a fool could see through his little scheme.

Li Luo shook his head helplessly. It wouldn't be right to just throw it away, so he politely accepted Liu Shaowen's letter.

After that, perhaps because the first two boys had given them enough courage, several other boys walked over to Ying Chanxi and delivered a letter.

Of course, to show they hadn't chosen Ying Chanxi just for her looks, many of the boys wrote one or two extra letters and gave them to other girls, or even boys.

But only the one for Ying Chanxi was likely the one they had spent the most ink and effort on.

Among them was even a second-year senior who approached Ying Chanxi, handed her his letter, and didn't forget to strike up a conversation with her.

"You're from Class One, right? I'm also from Class One, a year above you. You mentioned earlier that you joined the Math Club. If you have any questions about competitions, feel free to find me anytime."

"Okay, thank you." Ying Chanxi politely accepted the letter without any further reaction.

The second-year senior didn't linger. He smiled and left, but before he did, he glanced at Li Luo, a little curious about the boy's relationship with Ying Chanxi.

From what he'd heard one of the boys say to them earlier, it seemed he was some kind of cousin?

"What a bountiful harvest," Li Luo remarked, clucking his tongue as he looked at the pile of envelopes in front of Ying Chanxi. "All I've gotten is one letter from your classmate out of charity."

"Envious? Jealous?" Ying Chanxi huffed, then held out her hand to Li Luo and said, "Where's mine? Hurry up and give it to me."

"You already have so many, do you really need one more from me?"

"You talk too much." Ying Chanxi shot him a glare and leaned over impatiently to look at his two letters, scrutinizing them. "Which one is it?"

"Before you ask me for it, shouldn't you give me the letter you wrote for me first?"

"I already said it's not for you," Ying Chanxi insisted stubbornly, pulling back to pick up her pen and continue writing on the letter.

It was all the fault of those people who had interrupted her, making it so she still hadn't finished this letter.

Just then, on the other side of the classroom, Hua Xiuxiu finished her letter and handed one to Lin Yuan beside her, making him beam with joy.

Then, Hua Xiuxiu stood up, walked over to Li Luo, and held out a letter to him. "Class President, this is for you."

"Oh, thanks." Li Luo was a bit surprised. He took the letter from Hua Xiuxiu. "Sorry, I didn't prepare one for you."

"It's okay, this isn't to be pen pals," Hua Xiuxiu said with a smile. "It's just that there are some things on my mind that feel a bit hard to say to your face. It's much easier to write them in a letter."

"Then I'll accept it, thank you," Li Luo nodded, thanking her again.

Beside him, Ying Chanxi silently wrote, her hand gripping the pen a bit tighter. She pursed her lips and glanced at Hua Xiuxiu out of the corner of her eye, then looked back at Li Luo.

After Hua Xiuxiu left, she let out a dry laugh. "Is there a story?"

"It's probably a letter of repentance," Li Luo said casually as he put Hua Xiuxiu's envelope away.

"What letter of repentance?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback.

"Hmph," Li Luo snorted coldly. "Of course, it's a letter repenting for not running for Class President!"

"You're still holding on to that," Ying Chanxi said, a little speechless. Li Luo had complained about it during lunch, and she didn't expect him to still be hung up on it.

But Li Luo's interruption had somehow dissipated the small trace of emotion in her heart, so she turned back to continue writing her letter.

After spending a little more time, Ying Chanxi put the finished letter into an envelope, glanced at Li Luo beside her, then picked up the two sealed envelopes on her desk and stood up.

She ignored Li Luo and walked toward the front of the room.

The moment Ying Chanxi stood up, she instantly attracted the attention of many.

Many of the boys looked up curiously, wanting to see who Ying Chanxi would give her letters to.

Even the club president, Duan Qintian, instinctively looked over, a small sliver of hope sprouting in his heart.

Although he would have to step down and pass on the torch after National Day, that didn't stop him from becoming pen pals with someone.

There was no strict rule within the club that one had to find a pen pal within the club.

It was just that non-members of the Literature Club might not be as interested in having a pen pal.

In fact, Duan Qintian had only ever written one letter back in his first year, to the then-president Xu Youyu.

Unfortunately, Xu Youyu, who had received over a dozen letters at the time, hadn't replied to a single boy, and the matter was dropped.

Now, Ying Chanxi was walking straight toward the lectern, possessing looks and a presence that were in no way inferior to Xu Youyu's, which truly astounded even Duan Qintian.

And the boys who had given Ying Chanxi letters earlier felt their hearts hanging in suspense at this moment, their minds racing with possibilities, their hearts pounding violently.

Two letters.

Ying Chanxi was holding two letters!

Many people noticed this detail, thinking their own chances were still quite high.

Duan Qintian also watched with wide eyes as Ying Chanxi walked to the edge of the lectern, and he subconsciously swallowed.

But in the next second, he was disappointed.

Because Ying Chanxi reached out and, with a radiant smile, handed one of the letters in her hand to Xu Youyu, who was sitting in the front row.

"Senior, this is for you."

"Alright, thanks, Xixi." Xu Youyu took the envelope with a grin, then pulled a letter she had written herself from her desk drawer and handed it to Ying Chanxi. "This is mine, for you."

Seeing the way the two girls interacted, it seemed they already knew each other.

Expressions of realization appeared on the faces of those around them. Their gazes then fell on the remaining letter in Ying Chanxi's hand, and some of the boys' eyes even burned with intensity.

But just then, Xu Youyu, who had been sitting, suddenly stood up as well and pulled another letter from her desk drawer.

This time, even Duan Qintian raised an eyebrow in some surprise.

In his memory, aside from exchanging letters with girls in her class during her first year, Xu Youyu had never written a letter to anyone else.

But this time, besides giving one to the apparently long-acquainted Ying Chanxi, Xu Youyu had written another letter to give away?

The first-year students didn't understand the significance of this, but the second-year members knew it all too well.

Xu Youyu wasn't just the one and only golden flower of their Literature Club; she was also the vice president of the student council and would likely become president this year.

At the same time, she had consistently maintained her position as first in the grade, rarely ever being surpassed.

It was common for her Chinese compositions to receive high scores, and after every exam, her essays could be seen posted on the announcement board.

A girl like this had never before taken the initiative to write a letter to a boy.

Thinking of this, Duan Qintian couldn't help but guess that there must be another girl Xu Youyu knew among the first-year students.

As he was thinking this, Xu Youyu and Ying Chanxi were already walking together back in the direction Ying Chanxi had come from.

Almost everyone's eyes were fixed on the two graceful figures, staring intently at the envelopes in their hands.

Until the two of them stopped in front of Li Luo's desk and simultaneously held out their envelopes.

This single act shattered countless gazes in an instant.

"Here, take it," Ying Chanxi said casually, turning her head away.

"If I'm not in either of these two letters, you're dead meat." Xu Youyu looked at Li Luo with a beaming smile. After placing her own letter on his desk, she looked at the two letters Li Luo had written and spoke her extremely threatening words with a smile.

The entire classroom fell silent.

Only Li Luo rolled his eyes at the two of them, then nonchalantly picked up the two letters on his desk and handed them to Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu.

With the exchange completed, Xu Youyu nodded in satisfaction, gave him a look that said, "That's more like it," fanned herself with the envelope, and walked back to her seat.

Meanwhile, Ying Chanxi returned to her own seat, carefully placed Li Luo's letter in the inner pocket of her schoolbag, and then casually swept her arm across her desk, piling up the other envelopes and stuffing them all into her bag.

In the front row, Xu Youyu did much the same. She put the letters from Li Luo and Ying Chanxi away separately, while the letters from the other boys were shoved into her schoolbag and randomly piled up.

Li Luo wasn't so particular. After all, he had only received four letters in total. After putting them in his bag, he and Ying Chanxi stood up together and went to the lectern to bid farewell to the club president, Duan Qintian.

"Yes, if you have something to do, you can go ahead," Duan Qintian nodded at them, approving their request.

At the same time, Xu Youyu also packed her bag, said goodbye to Duan Qintian, and headed out of the classroom.

Just then, Qin Yawei, who was at the side, suddenly stood up, walked over to Li Luo, and tucked a letter into his arms.

"Here, take this," Qin Yawei said, after glancing at Xu Youyu.

Li Luo blinked, taking the letter from the vice president, still not quite understanding the situation. Under the gazes of Ying Chanxi, Xu Youyu, and many other students, all he could do was say politely, "Thank you, Senior Qin."

Beside him, Ying Chanxi silently stared at Qin Yawei for a few seconds without saying another word, then turned and walked out of the classroom.

Then, under the envious and jealous stares of many boys, Li Luo followed Ying Chanxi out.

(End of Chapter)
